newsitem.title: UK: OPEC oil output at 16-year high in January says survey. [CORRECTED 20:42 GMT]
newsitem.headline: OPEC oil output at 16-year high in January says survey. [CORRECTED 20:42 GMT]

text.p: OPEC output hit a 16-year high in January, swollen by Iraq's first full month of exports under the United Nations oil-for-food exchange, a Reuters survey of industry experts said Thursday.

Crude oil production from the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries rose 300,000 barrels per day to 26.64 million last month from a revised 26.34 million in December, the survey of oil analysts, OPEC delegates and company officials found.

OPEC, pumping an extra 600,000 barrels a day in the past two months, looks set to add more oil as foreign companies, bringing new fields onstream, seek to cash in on their investments, OPEC monitors said.
"I see OPEC heading to 27 million barrels per day by the middle of the year -- easily," said Mehdi Varzi, director of research for energy at brokerage house Kleinwort Benson Securities.
OPEC's official output ceiling is a combined 25.033 million barrels a day for the 11-member cartel.
Iraq's output, boosted by some 500,000 barrels of exports, rose 190,000 to 1.12 million barrels in January, according to the survey.
Baghdad has found no difficulty in selling its oil after quickly wrapping up some 25 contracts with buyers from Asia, Europe and the United States.
Most OPEC countries continued to ignore official output quotas leaving rising demand to absorb extra supplies without any adverse impact on prices.
January saw small output increases from Nigeria and Qatar for the third month in succession as new foreign company operated fields build toward full capacity.
Nigeria was pegged at 2.1 million barrels a day, 235,000 barrels above its quota, aided by rising production from two long-term joint ventures with Mobil Corp. and Chevron Corp. and Canada's Abacan.
Qatar pumped 550,000 barrels a day, or 163,000 over quota, with the help of the new Al-Rayyan field that is operated by Atlantic Richfield Co.

Even the United Arab Emirates appeared to stretch its output in January. The UAE is one of only a trio of core Middle East producers, with OPEC kingpin Saudi Arabia and Kuwait, seen holding any extra capacity.
But monitors saw 2.25 million barrels a day from the UAE in January, some 90,000 in excess of its official allocation.
Saudi Arabia maintained output at quota in January, running at 8.01 million.
With more than 2 million barrels a day of capacity in mothballs, Saudi policy will remain key to the fortunes of the oil markets this year.
But there is no sign from the Kingdom that it intends to dip into its spare capacity reserve.
"Having enjoyed the fruits of restraint in the oil price rise of 1996 I think they'll be loathe to jeopardise similar returns in 1997," said Kleinwort's Varzi.
Venezuela kept its production running high, at 3.17 million in January, hugely in excess of its 2.36 million quota.
